purpose: Test whether draining a timed-out optional unit and terminating its MPS client process removes the residual tail observed when the CUDA context remained idle.

selection_source.confirm29: Admission quarantine with an idle live CUDA context produced one 38.011 ms RAN miss in 10000 releases.
selection_source.policy_change: After the first timeout, drain the physical work, reject its result, send stop, close the RPC channel, wait for process exit, and never admit that endpoint again.

fault.work_unit: 40 sequential NeuralRx CUDA Graph launches in a separate low-priority MPS client
fault.post_timeout_policy: drain and reject the late response, stop the worker, close the client channel, wait for process exit, and issue no later work

interpretation_limit: Passing supports fail-closed recovery for the tested A100/MPS workload and D35 contract. It does not prove universal hard real-time isolation or preemption of an already running CUDA kernel.
